output.brief: The rejections were most likely caused by a setting error in our own paperwork. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation system, the mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record. It carried 7.0°C instead of our 4.0°C specification. All five Meridane containers sailed at 7.0°C and were all rejected. The four containers on the email template at 4.0°C, including three on Coastway and one early Meridane, were accepted. Carrier controller data shows the units held their setpoint, so Meridane did not fail, and a refrigeration claim would likely fail. The fungicide does not explain it: Pellacor fruit passed at 4°C, and K3 was rejected on old stock. Lower Serra fruit decayed somewhat more, but it was a minor factor, and suspending those growers would punish the wrong party. Next steps: correct the mandarin record to 4.0°C now, and have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check comparing reefer settings against the product specification before submission. Hold the claim, the suspension, the supplier reversal and any deduction from Brindle's invoice. I'm quite confident, though Lower Serra's smaller effect is not fully explained.
